summary: Lynn Thomas is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a BA and MA from Lancaster University and a D.Phil from the University of Oxford by 1987. She served as a lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton (attested 1997).

László Gaál was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological linguistics. He earned a Ph.D. at Franz Joseph University and studied at Göttingen under Friedrich Carl Andreas, Gyula Németh, János Csengeri, Emil Sieg, and Richard Fick. He later held posts at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Debrecen.

Léon Feer was a French scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes under Foucaux, Pavie, Mohl, and Quatremère. He held posts at INALCO, Collège de France, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Bibliothèque nationale de France.
Léon Rodet was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the École Polytechnique from circa 1851 to 1853 and was a member of the Société Asiatique from circa 1865 to 1895.

Léon Vandermeersch was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at INALCO, EPHE, and the University of Paris. His career included roles at the National Museum of Vietnamese History, Aix-Marseille University, Paris Diderot University, EPHE, Maison Franco-Japonaise, and Director of EFEO (1989–1993).

Léonard Eugène Aurousseau was a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at EPHE and INALCO under Édouard Chavannes between 1908 and 1911. From 1909 he was affiliated with the École française d'Extrême-Orient, serving as its Director from 1926 to 1929.

Lê Mạnh Thát is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Saigon (BA, circa 1962–1965) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD, circa 1965–1974), and held a post at Vạn Hạnh University (circa 1974–1975).

M. A. Mehendale was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Joint Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (attested 1955) and had a long career at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute as Professor of Sanskrit and Vedic literature (attested 1970–2026).
M. Athar Ali was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Aligarh Muslim University from circa 1948 to 1953 and later worked there as a historian from circa 1954 to 1990.

M. D. Balasubrahmanyam is an Indologist and linguist who completed his dissertation at Savitribai Phule Pune University. He held posts at Pune University (attested 1967), Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha, and as Principal at Rashtriya Sanskrit Sansthan's Sri Sadashiva Campus (attested 1973).

M. H. Krishna was an Indologist and historian who studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, University of Madras, and University College London under Ernest Arthur Gardner and others. He spent his career at the University of Mysore, including serving as Dean of Arts.

M. M. McCabe is a philosopher who studied at Newnham College and the University of Cambridge. She served as a Fellow at Murray Edwards College (1981–1990), Professor at King's College London (1990–2014), and Keeling Scholar and Honorary Professor at UCL (circa 2014).

M. R. Raghava Varier is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Calicut, the Archaeological Survey of India, and Jawaharlal Nehru University. He later served as a professor at the University of Calicut.

M. S. A. Rao was an Indology and sociology scholar. He studied at the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye and at the University of Delhi, later holding posts at Delhi (circa 1959–1985), Syracuse University, and the University of Pennsylvania.

M. S. Nagaraja Rao was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Mysore and Savitribai Phule Pune University under M. N. Deshpande. He worked at Karnatak University, Karnataka State Archaeology Department, and served as Director General of the ASI (1984–1987).

M. Seshagiri Sastri was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Presidency College, Chennai, Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library (attested 1899), and Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency University (attested 1899).

M. Shinoda is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He also attended Agoura High School (circa 1991–1995) and the Art Center College of Design (circa 1995–1998).

M. Victor Stanley was a linguistics and Indology scholar. He studied at Lawrence University, the University of Wisconsin-Madison (BA), the University of Oregon (MA), and Yale University (PhD, circa 1894–1895), and served as Supervising-Principal for Corona-Norco Unified School District.

M. Yamunacharya was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Mysore Hiriyanna, Ardeshir Ruttonji Wadia, and Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. He served as Professor of Philosophy at Maharaja's College, Mysore.

M.L. Pattaratorn Chirapravati is a scholar of Buddhist studies and art history. Educated at Silpakorn, Ohio State, and Cornell universities, she has held posts at Silpakorn, Tsukuba, the Asian Art Museum, Sonoma State, California State University, Sacramento, Yale-NUS, and NTU.
